source.title: Long-range neural and gap junction protein-mediated cues control polarity during planarian regeneration.
source.location: Results text, section 'Long-range information is provided to wounded areas through the ventral nerve cord and gap junctions' (Figure 1B; '>95% single-head (normal) animals'); dose from Methods

stage: fragments retaining the original head region (various transverse cut levels)
injury: transverse amputations along the A/P axis, original head region retained

intervention.timing: fragments transferred into octanol immediately after amputation
intervention.duration: 3 days (exposure length stated for the Fig 5 / Discussion octanol treatment; Fig S1B schedule not on disk)
intervention.description: Fragments that keep the original head region soaked in 127 uM octanol from amputation

readout.method: macroscopic observation of regenerates with CNS marker staining

notes: Text gives '>95% single-head (normal)'; 95 used as the stated bound and the remaining <=5% (not described; Fig 1B legend says 'very few' bipolar-head regenerates) placed in 'other'. n not stated. Octanol 127 uM from Methods; 3-day duration taken from the Fig 5 legend/Discussion statement of the octanol exposure (medium confidence).

adjudication.note: A gave normal 95 only; remainder added to other so percentages sum to 100

notes: Text: inverted A/P axis and bipolar head in 20% of pharyngeal fragments, n=21. 20% x 21 = 4.2 -> 4 (4/21 = 19%; the stated % does not map exactly to an integer). The other 17 are not described ('other' = not characterised; may include normal regenerates).

source.title: Long-range neural and gap junction protein-mediated cues control polarity during planarian regeneration.
source.location: Figure 4A legend ('In all cases (n>90) treated animals developed A/P polarity problems') and Results text (posterior-facing wounds section)

injury: transverse post-pharyngeal amputation plus one or two simultaneous lateral cuts

intervention.timing: fragments transferred into octanol immediately after amputation
intervention.duration: 3 days (exposure length stated for the Fig 5 / Discussion octanol treatment; Fig S1B schedule not on disk)
intervention.description: Post-pharyngeal fragments given one or two lateral cuts and soaked in 127 uM octanol

readout.method: macroscopic observation of regenerates with CNS marker staining

notes: All treated lateral-cut fragments (n>90, a bound, so n_total null) had A/P polarity problems: bipolar, triple or quadruple heads, not split by number in text. Mixed multi-head counts go to 'other' (= two, three or four heads). Legend adds that ~20% of a VNC-disrupting subset (n=38) formed anterior structures in all 4 blastemas; that subset overlaps this arm and is not written as a separate row.

adjudication.note: A wrote only the overlapping ~20% (n=38) four-head subset; kept the whole-arm row and folded the subset into notes
